title: Static Litany
summary: Storm season cracks choir-glass if it rides rough, and the temple's great horn is deaf until its new pane arrives. Pem has annealed a fresh sheet in the glass chapel's old burn and needs it carried down through a closing storm window — unbroken, unhurried, and, ideally, unlistened-to.

objectives.label: Lift annealed choir-glass from the glass chapel racks
Set the pane at the temple steps before the window seals
Hold position while Pem reads the storm off the glass

offer.text: Station. The storm season has opinions, and this week it expressed them through our great horn. The pane is *shattered*, and a deaf horn hears nothing. Hearing nothing, station, is worse than it sounds.

A new sheet has been annealing in the chapel burn since yesterday. Choir-glass keeps the memory of every vibration of its cooling. If it rides rough, it cools *wrong* — and then it will only ever sing the road, and never the voice.
You want me to carry a six-foot pane of haunted glass across the desert, gently, against the clock, while a storm tries to lean on it.
When you say it, it sounds like faith. Good. Carry it like faith, station.

accept.text: The window between the walls is four, perhaps five minutes of clean air. My radio will count you down in its way. If the glass begins to hum a note you did not give it — do not hum back.
The Hollow is lighting every lamp for your road, courier. The glass knows the way home. We merely ask you not to drop home.
Ketch here. Choir-glass on a hover-bike in storm season. I've seen worse ideas — Rill's full of them — but smooth hands, kid. Drift the bends, don't fight them. Cracks come from *surprise*.

complete.text: Whole. Not spider-webbed, not sung. Station — do you know how rare it is that anything crosses that desert *whole*? The glass is cooling on the horn now and it is… oh. Oh, listen.

It kept a memory of the storm anyway — not the crashing, the *counting*. It cooled with the rhythm in it. Forty years of notebooks, station, and this pane just indexed itself. I shall call it a litany. The Choir will call it a hymn. The storms will call it, eventually, *back*.
It's playing my ride? The brake dip at the chapel gate, the drift over the slick — I can hear my own line in it. That's… keep the volume low, Warden.
Low, yes. But never off. The courier's part is written into the glass now, station. Whatever is waking out there — it knows a Driftline engine note when it hears one.
